written_before: the smoke re-run that tests this change (40 bees, 30 s, non-prereg) and any run with N >= 100

change.loadgen_readiness_barrier: Before its first task submission, the loadgen waits until both of its own subscriptions (its reply topic and task.done) have delivered a probe. The probes are harness messages, not tasks: a probe on the reply topic has a taskId that begins with 'probe-' and is not counted, not written to the JSONL, and not part of any percentile. A probe on task.done has hostId '__probe__', so both hosts ignore it. Probes are re-sent once per second until both are seen, with a 60 s limit. The load clock (startMs, and therefore the kill time for LoadStart) starts after the barrier.
change.reason: With topics pre-created (MESH_SCALE_prereg_amendment_2.json), the smoke run N=40 decomposition showed the host-to-bee-to-host leg in the first 5 s at p50 140 ms, down from 2528 ms. The remaining early delay was in the submit-plus-reply leg, p50 3603 ms in 0-5 s, and it falls back to 57 ms in 5-10 s. The loadgen's reply consumer is a new group that joins at load start, so replies to the first seconds wait for partition assignment. That is a measurement-client warm-up artifact, not a mesh behaviour. Under the pre-registered population, a task submitted at time t is counted from t, so the barrier is the only way to start the clock with the client ready.
what_is_not_changed: the task population: every task after the barrier is counted and none is excluded
rates, durations, bee and host counts, Xmx values, latencies, heartbeat, attempt timeout, tier, kill fraction and kill timing (still relative to load start)
Host, Registry and BeeAgent routing and retry behaviour, and the publish error handling of the mesh

still_open_for_the_lead: Host ignores the future returned by bus.publish. A failed assignment or TaskDone is recovered only by the attempt timeout (10 s). The smoke runs show Kafka 'Error publishing' lines from host JVMs. That is a mesh issue and needs its own decision and amendment. It is not changed here.

Expected effect of the barrier: the 0-5 s overhead should fall to the steady-state range, so the verdict of A2 at N=1000 should depend on the steady state, not on the startup. The smoke re-run will show whether that is so.
